name: Top notes in the diff's columns

pr.title: Line up a file's top notes with its diff, and show a lone pull request as a stack of one
pr.head: 8b260234bba8646a1beffb3979dac8489be11f93

summary: A summary page is the guided review page that project summary publish puts on a repository's Projector site. Each file on the page is a card: a header, an optional one-line description, the notes about the file, and then its diff as one table per hunk. A note is a reviewer's remark, tagged context, verified, or concern. A note can sit under one line of the diff or at the top of the card, about the whole file.

Notes under a line already render as rows of the diff table, with the tag in the line-number gutter and the text where the code starts. Notes at the top of a card were a separate bulleted list, so their tags and text lined up with nothing below them. This pull request makes the top notes the same kind of row, in a small table that shares the diff's columns, so every note on the card lines up.
It also makes three smaller changes to the same page:

• A stack of one. The sidebar lists every pull request in a stack, one row each, with the current one highlighted. A pull request with no stack showed only its title in grey. It now shows the same list with one highlighted row. The build's data does not change: only the page draws the row.
  • More room around notes. Note rows get 9px of padding above and below their text instead of 5px.
  • Notes, not Review notes. A section's list of notes is headed Notes, and the page's "How to read this" paragraph says "Notes come in three kinds".

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Card: one file's block on the summary page, rendered by renderFile.
  • Top notes: the notes on a whole file, with no line. The code calls them loose.
  • Note row: a tr.noterow, with the tag in the gutter cell td.ngut and the text in td.nte.
  • Stack: the chain of pull requests whose bases are each other's heads. The build stores it as data.stack, empty for a pull request that stands alone.

groups.title: The page renderer
groups.kicker: Top notes become note rows in the diff's columns, and a lone pull request gets a one-row stack.
intro: The summary renderer, site/src/summary.ts, builds the whole page in the browser from the summary's data. renderFile draws one card per file. Before this change it drew a note under a line as a table row inside the diff, and drew the top notes through notesList, the same bulleted list a section uses for its own notes.

Now renderFile has one function, noteRow, that turns any note into a table row. The diff's rows call it for notes under a line, and the top notes go through it into a separate table placed above the diff. That table gets the same class and the same <colgroup> as the diff's hunk tables, so its gutter is exactly as wide as theirs. A diff that shows only one side, such as a new file, has one wide gutter column instead of two, and the top table follows it.

The stylesheet loses the padding and font size that the old list needed, since the diff table's note-row rules now apply. It also drops the .prtitle rule, which only the old lone-pull-request title used.

checks.text: The compiled site/assets/summary.js is the TypeScript's build output and ships with the change. Rebuilding it at this head produced no difference.

files.note: Adds noteRow and the top-notes table in renderFile, renames the section heading, and makes stackList fall back to a one-row stack.

checks.text: A concern note's checkbox is keyed by the file's path, as it was when notesList(loose, 'fnotes', f.path) drew the top notes, so a concern a reader already checked stays checked. The checkbox handler marks box.closest('li, tr'), so it finds the new rows. I traced both in the code.
The top table holds no tr.add, tr.del, or tr.ctx rows and no .src spans, so syntax highlighting and token marking, which read only those, leave it alone. I traced highlightFile and the token marker.
The table keeps the fnotes class, so the stylesheet's rules for collapsed and reviewed files still remove its border and hide it.

stackList uses data.stack only when it lists two or more pull requests. Otherwise it draws one current row from the pull request itself. The current row returns before it reads url, so the empty url is never used. A test checks the rendered row.

files.note: Lets the diff's note-row rules style the top notes, widens note-row padding to 9px, and drops the unused .prtitle rule.

checks.text: This padding applies to every note row, both under a line and at the top of a card.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: Two node-rendered tests cover the new markup, and the CLI reference names the stack of one.
intro: FileHeaderTests in tests/test_site.py builds a summary and renders it with the compiled script under node. One test now gives a file a note on the whole file and checks that it renders as a note row in a diff fnotes table with the diff's columns. A new test checks that a pull request with an empty stack shows one highlighted row in the sidebar. Both skip when node is missing.
docs/cli.md describes the site's sidebar, and gains a clause saying that a pull request alone is a stack of one.

checks.text: The expected markup pins the exact column group: two lncol columns for a file with both sides.
